_note: Story dialogues. {merchant}, {rival}, {player}, {cargo}, {gift_text} are filled in from the campaign. A check option rolls D20 + attribute against dc, then jumps to its success or fail node. 'once' hides a check after it has been tried.

hello.text: Good harvest this year. Roads have been packed with carts since morning.

options.label: How is trade with the {rival} kingdom?
Something about your cargo smells off…

supplies.text: Rope, salt, lamp oil. Coin first, friend. I've {cargo} too, but I'm not selling that to you.

rival.text: {rival}? They dig stone and sell it dear. There's a grey rock in the hills between you and them that nobody has claimed yet. Won't stay that way.

gift.text: …Fine. You have a nose. These are {cargo}. They won't last to market. Take them before the road eats them. Your people will thank you, if you get them home.

offended.text: Smells off? My cargo? I'll have you know… well. Never mind. Ask the {rival} hills about smells. They're sitting on stone they haven't even claimed.

arrive.text: A ring of broken pillars. One stone still stands, covered in carved lines that might be letters, or a map.

options.label: Walk the ring and look for what doesn't fit

map.text: Under a loose slab: an oiled leather case. Inside, a surveyor's map. Three places are marked that you have never seen.

lost.text: You read the lines as a path and follow it into the woods. It was not a path. By the time you are back, it is dark.

nothing.text: Stones, moss, a fox den. Whatever is here, it isn't showing itself to you today.

demand.text: Our scouts saw your banner on the grey rock. That stone has fed {rival} walls for three generations. Take your flag down, or pay us thirty gold for the insult.

options.label: Pay the thirty gold from the treasury
Why fight over it? Buy the stone from us.

paid.text: Wise. We will tell our council you are reasonable people.

refused.text: Then {rival} will remember this. Not today, not tomorrow. But we will remember.

deal.text: …Buy it. Hm. Five stone a week, fifteen gold. Our masons would rather work than fight. Done.
deal.stamp: Trade deal: 5 Stone → 15 Gold every week

hello.text: A {player} banner, this far from home? Ships don't wait, so talk fast.

options.label: Our wagons could meet your ships. A standing trade.

news.text: Pirates south, storms east. And a captain swears there's iron in the cliffs up the coast. Nobody's had the nerve to dig.

trade.text: You talk like a merchant's daughter. Fine. Two gold a day, every day, for grain and timber. Shake on it.

busy.text: Come back when you have something on a cart, not in your mouth.

hello.text: Another southerner looking at my swords like they're bread. These are for people who can lift them.

who.text: Anyone with stone or coin. Mostly stone. You southerners never have stone.

won.text: Ha! Ow. Fine. Take this one, it's yours. Tell nobody.

lost.text: That's what I thought. Come back when you've eaten more bread.

hello.text: Sit. The kettle's on. It's bitter, mind. Most people spit it out.

options.label: What do you see in me?

strong.text: Ha. You kept it down. Good. It'll keep you up, too.

spit.text: They all spit. Here, wipe your chin.

seen.text: Someone who listens better than they fight. Use it. There are places on this map that only a listener finds.

unseen.text: Mud on your boots. That's all I see today.
